**STEP 1 - Scene:** A snack, not a full meal: a small pile of orange cheese-flavoured triangular tortilla chips (Doritos-style) on a white plate.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A white square-ish side plate, about 20 cm across. Area = 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm². The plate at the bottom edge belongs to another setting and is excluded.

**STEP 3 - Items:** Orange triangular corn chips (about 6 pieces, plus a few crumbs). No oil, dip or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The chips cover roughly 17% of the plate, about 53 cm². Crumbs are negligible.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Chips are thin, but the overlapping pile is about 0.6 cm tall on average. 53 cm² × 0.6 cm ≈ 32 ml gross.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Chips are very airy, so I use a bulk density of about 0.35 g/ml (a snack-chip value, outside the listed categories). 32 ml × 0.35 ≈ 11 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cheese-flavoured corn chips are about 490 kcal/100 g. 11 g × 4.9 ≈ 54 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Six to eight chips at about 1.5 g each is roughly 9–12 g, so 11 g is plausible. A few hundred kcal would be far too high for this amount of food.

**Total:** about 11 g, about 54 kcal.
